stem: Group 17 elements are commonly referred to as the halogens.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State and explain the trend in volatility of chlorine, bromine and iodine down the group.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Hydrogen gas reacts with the different halogens under different conditions.
parts.text: State the conditions required for chlorine to react with hydrogen at room temperature.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
On heating, iodine reacts with hydrogen in a reversible reaction.

Give the equation for this reaction. Include state symbols.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
In this reaction, one of the reactants behaves as a Brønsted-Lowry acid.

What is meant by the term Brønsted-Lowry acid?

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the reactant behaving as an acid and its conjugate base.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Name the type of bond formed between $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to make $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: For $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$, predict its shape and the $\text{H}-\text{O}-\text{H}$ bond angle.
